_README.what: The Permanent Injury Table: one hundred hand-authored d100 rows, worst at 1 and best at 100.
_README.when: Roll it when the fiction calls for a lasting consequence: after surviving death saves (the Injury Desk and Wario's Casino hand off to it, skipping row 1), after a Casino sentence, or whenever the GM says so.
_README.contract: Exactly 100 rows, d100 1-100 in order, categories in the band order below, every injuryType unique, no roll numerals. `cure` is the LOWEST rung of the ladder that removes the row; `duration` is how long it lasts without that cure. Field names are read live by index.html (#/injuries, character injury panels), the Casino drum, the standalone desk and tools/generate-injury-table.py — do not rename them.
_README.status: authored and locked. The old machine-generated table (343 rows, mostly 'Veilbound Vein' template repeats, later culled to 204) was wiped on 2026-10-04 and replaced by this one. The genkit `injury-table` generator is retired and refuses to write a locked table; edit this file by hand and run `python3 tools/generate-injury-table.py --check`.
_README.mechanics: Fifth-edition vocabulary: advantage/disadvantage, exhaustion levels, the Dash action, death saving throws, hit point maximum, DCs for Wisdom (Medicine). Spell names are the cure ladder. A GM overrides any row the fiction or the player's comfort requires.
_README.references: Setting hooks in notes are to filed canon only: Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic (dr_toads_star_hill_clinic), the Menders (Liberated Toads healer cohort), the Mages' Guild, Toadstool Tonic, the 1-Up Mushroom.

title: Permanent Injury Table
description: A d100 table for injuries that outlast the fight. Low is worse: 1 is death, the twenties are the body never being the same, the fifties heal in weeks, the nineties are the luck of the survivor. Every row names its lowest cure and how long it lasts without one.
rules: A result is a story consequence, not a replacement for a GM ruling. Reroll or override anything that would ruin the table's fun or a player's night.
Roll d100 straight. The Injury Desk's death-save handoff and the Casino's survival roll skip row 1 (Death), because the saves already answered that question.
Low is worse. Rows 1-56 are the price of surviving; 57-70 are a bad week; 71-92 are marks, trauma and oddities; 93-100 are the luck of the survivor.
The cure listed is the LOWEST rung that removes the row. Anything stronger on the ladder works too: Regenerate fixes everything Greater Restoration fixes, a 1-Up Mushroom fixes everything.
Rows that say 'treat as' another row borrow that row's mechanics, never its cure.
A character record references a result by d100 in its injuries array (see docs/INJURY_TABLE_GUIDE.md). The effect text lives here, once.

cureLadder.means: Time alone; the duration says how long. Bed, food and nobody hitting you.
A healer with a kit and the stated Wisdom (Medicine) DC — Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic, a Mender, or a party member with the proficiency — followed by the stated weeks.
Second-level magic: blindness, deafness, disease, poison, and the table's infections and short-term injuries.
Third-level magic. Quiets the table's special effects even though none of them is formally a curse.
Fifth-level magic: hit point maximum, nerve damage, exhaustion that will not lift, and the mental trauma band when a season of care is not available.
Sixth-level magic: cures the throat, the eyes and the ears and knits any broken bone at once.
Seventh-level magic: regrows limbs, eyes, organs and skin. In this kingdom that means the Mages' Guild, a Potion of Regeneration, or a favour nobody should owe.
Row 1 only. The 1-Up works on the spot; Raise Dead has ten days; Resurrection has a century.

entries.description: The blow was simply more than the body. You die now, where you fall — no death saving throws, no last words unless the GM is feeling generous.
entries.cure: Raise Dead within ten days; Resurrection after that; a 1-Up Mushroom on the spot.
entries.notes: If this row comes up off the death-save handoff, the saves already answered the question — reroll. The Casino's survival roll and the Injury Desk both skip it there.

entries.description: Something in you has one fewer chance left. From now on two failed death saving throws kill you, not three.
entries.notes: The cruellest permanent row. Tell the player plainly and write it on the sheet where the whole table can see it.

entries.description: Death found the way in once and remembers it. Whenever you drop to 0 hit points you begin with one failed death saving throw already marked.

Your blood will not clot. While you are dying, a Wisdom (Medicine) check cannot stabilise you — only a healer's kit or magic can — and any damage you take at 0 hit points counts as two failed death saves.
entries.notes: Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic and the Menders can treat each episode, not the condition.

entries.description: Severed or crushed past saving, at the shoulder, on the side you fight with. You cannot use two-handed weapons or a shield together with a weapon, and Strength (Athletics) checks that need two hands — climbing, grappling, hauling — are made at disadvantage.
entries.notes: A smith-made prosthesis restores carrying and steadying, not weapon work or fine manipulation.

entries.description: The off-side arm is gone at the shoulder. No shields, no two-handed weapons, no two-weapon fighting; one-handed fighting and somatic components are unaffected.

Taken at the wrist. You cannot fight with two weapons or use a two-handed weapon, and checks with thieves' tools or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) are made at disadvantage. A fitted hook or clamp lets you strap on a shield.

Above the knee. On a crutch your speed is 5 feet; with a fitted peg or prosthesis it is 20 feet and you cannot take the Dash action. Dexterity saving throws and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks are made at disadvantage.
entries.notes: Mounts, carts and a strong friend's shoulder all still work. The Menders fit pegs; a good one takes a fortnight to learn.

entries.description: Gone at the ankle. Your speed is reduced by 10 feet (5 feet with a fitted prosthesis), and Strength (Athletics) checks to run or jump and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to balance are made at disadvantage.

Two or three fingers from one hand. The grip holds, but you cannot draw a bow (crossbows are fine) and checks with thieves' tools, an instrument, or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) are made at disadvantage.
One eye is gone. You have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight and on ranged attack rolls against targets more than 30 feet away.
entries.notes: An eyepatch, obviously.

entries.description: You can speak only in a rasping whisper that carries about 10 feet. Spells with verbal components still work, but Charisma checks that depend on your voice — Persuasion, Performance, Intimidation — are made at disadvantage.

One lung never reinflated properly. You can hold your breath for half the usual time, and whenever you take the Dash action on two consecutive turns you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of exhaustion.
entries.notes: Greater Restoration removes the exhaustion but not the lung.

entries.description: The spine took it. Your speed is halved, you cannot take the Dash action, you cannot wear heavy armour, and Dexterity saving throws are made at disadvantage.
entries.notes: A season in the Menders' care gets most people from a chair to a cane; the GM may lift the Dash ban after that, not the rest.

entries.description: The joint was reassembled from pieces. Your speed is reduced by 10 feet, you can take the Dash action only once per combat, and Dexterity (Acrobatics) and climbing checks are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Treatment — a surgeon's reset (DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine)) followed by eight weeks off it; Greater Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: The hand is there but the tendons are not: it can hold, it cannot grip. Treat it as Lost Hand (07) for weapons, tools and Sleight of Hand.
entries.cure: Treatment — a surgeon's repair (DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine)) and six weeks splinted; Greater Restoration ends it at once.
entries.notes: Cheaper to fix than an amputation, which is the only good news.

entries.description: A third of your skin is scar now. Your hit point maximum is reduced by 1d8 (rolled once), and Constitution saving throws against heat, fire and exhaustion from heat are made at disadvantage.
entries.notes: Greater Restoration restores the hit points; only Regenerate gives the skin back.

entries.description: Something was damaged that no bandage reaches. Your hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to your level.
entries.notes: Dr. Toad can keep it from getting worse. He will say so, cheerfully, and mean it.

entries.description: Your speed is reduced by 10 feet, you cannot take the Dash action, and Dexterity saving throws are made at disadvantage. Stairs are a decision.
entries.cure: Treatment — a surgeon's reset (DC 18 Wisdom (Medicine)) and twelve weeks in a bed; Regenerate ends it at once.

entries.description: The arm is still attached and the nerves are not. It hangs. Treat it as Lost Arm, Off Side (06) — or Weapon Side (05) if that is the one it took.
entries.notes: Nerve, not bone: cheaper to cure than an amputation, and it looks exactly as bad.

entries.description: The wound has turned and keeps turning. At each dawn make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw; on a failure your hit point maximum drops by 1d6 until cured. Three failures in a row and the limb has to come off (roll 05-10).
entries.cure: Lesser Restoration, or Treatment — a healer with a kit succeeding on a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check on three consecutive days.
entries.duration: Until cured; the lost hit points return with Greater Restoration or a month of real rest.
entries.notes: Fatal in a season if ignored. Nobody ignores it twice.

entries.description: The head took a blow it should not have survived. Intelligence and Wisdom checks are made at disadvantage, and whenever you take a critical hit you must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.
Both eardrums burst. You are deafened: you automatically fail checks that require hearing, and you cannot hear your allies' warnings. You can still speak, so verbal components work.
One ear is a wall of silence and ringing. Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing are made at disadvantage, and you cannot tell which direction a sound came from.
entries.cure: Rest — six weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Burned by light, acid or sand. You are blinded.
entries.notes: Without magic, a clinic can save some sight in 2d4 weeks; the GM may then downgrade this to Lost Eye (11) or Clouded Eye (46).

entries.description: Every breath is a negotiation. Strength (Athletics) checks and Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration are made at disadvantage, and you cannot take the Dash action.
entries.cure: Rest — four weeks, bound; Heal or Regenerate ends it at once.

entries.description: Splinted and slow. Your speed is halved and you cannot take the Dash action.
entries.cure: Rest — six weeks (eight if no healer set it within a day); Heal or Regenerate ends it at once.
entries.duration: Six to eight weeks, or until cured.

entries.description: In a sling and useless. You cannot use that arm: no shield, no two-handed weapon, no two-weapon fighting. Somatic components work with the other hand.
entries.cure: Rest — six weeks; Heal or Regenerate ends it at once.

entries.description: The world is slightly to the left of where you reach for it. Intelligence checks, Wisdom checks and Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration are made at disadvantage, and a second blow to the head while concussed knocks you unconscious for 1 minute.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks, in the dark if possible; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Dislocated, and the joint tore on the way out. You cannot raise that arm above the shoulder: attack rolls with two-handed weapons and Strength (Athletics) checks to climb are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Treatment — a healer resetting it (DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine)) and four weeks strapped; Greater Restoration ends it at once.
entries.duration: Four weeks once set; permanent until cured if it is never set.

entries.description: The bones are gravel in a splint. For the duration the hand cannot grip anything: treat it as Lost Hand (07).
entries.cure: Rest — six weeks; Heal or Regenerate ends it at once.

entries.description: Infection is waiting in it. Until cured you regain no hit points from spending Hit Dice, and at the end of each long rest you must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of exhaustion.
entries.cure: Lesser Restoration, or Treatment — a healer with a kit succeeding on a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check on three consecutive days.

entries.description: The nerve to the fingers was cut. Checks with thieves' tools, Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks and attack rolls with finesse weapons held in that hand are made at disadvantage.
A tendon healed short. Your speed is reduced by 5 feet and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Treatment — a surgeon lengthening the tendon (DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine)) and eight weeks off it; Greater Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: A tremor that never fully stops. Ranged attack rolls and any check that needs steady hands — lockpicking, surgery, lettering, pouring a potion into someone else — are made at disadvantage.

It skips when it is frightened, and it is frightened by pain. Whenever you take 15 or more damage from a single source you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or be incapacitated until the end of your next turn.

The old break never stopped talking. Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration are made at disadvantage, and after any forced march or night without a bed you have disadvantage on all ability checks until you finish a long rest.
entries.notes: Toadstool Tonic and similar take the edge off for an evening. They do not cure it.

entries.description: Smoke, spores or Bowser's breath. You cannot hold your breath for more than one round, and Constitution saving throws against inhaled poisons and gases are made at disadvantage.
Attack rolls and ability checks that use that hand are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Your speed is reduced by 10 feet.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Strength (Athletics) checks and Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — three weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Stitched, badly, in the field. Whenever you roll a 1 on an attack roll or a Strength (Athletics) check the stitches tear and you take 1d4 damage.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: You gain two levels of exhaustion. A long rest removes only one of them per day, and the first will not lift without a full meal.
entries.cure: Rest and food — two long rests; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: The bone is cracked, not broken, and it reminds you. Attack rolls with two-handed weapons and Strength checks to lift or drag are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — three weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Bandaged to the wrist. You can hold a weapon or a shield and nothing fiddlier: no somatic components, no thieves' tools, and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: One eye sees shapes and light, not detail. Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — four weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.
entries.notes: If it has not cleared in a season it will not: convert to Lost Eye (11).

entries.description: Your speed is reduced by 5 feet and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to balance are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — four weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: You cannot carry more than half your carrying capacity, and Strength checks are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Popped back in, but it clicks and aches. Charisma (Persuasion) and Charisma (Performance) checks are made at disadvantage and you can eat only soft food. Verbal components are unaffected.
entries.cure: Rest — one week; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Whatever bit you was not clean. At each dawn make a DC 11 Constitution saving throw; on a failure you gain one level of exhaustion that rest will not remove until the infection is gone.
entries.cure: Lesser Restoration, or Treatment — a healer with a kit succeeding on a DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine) check on three consecutive days.

entries.description: Constitution saving throws are made at disadvantage, and you regain hit points from only half your Hit Dice during a short rest.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Half the ear is hanging by a flap. Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing are made at disadvantage while it heals; when it has healed it is notched for good.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.
entries.duration: Two weeks, or until cured; the notch is permanent.

entries.description: The knee gives without warning. You have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws, and standing up from prone costs all of your movement.
entries.cure: Rest — three weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: You cannot catch your breath. You cannot take the Dash action on two consecutive turns, and Constitution checks for sustained exertion are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — two weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: You breathe through your mouth and sleep like a sawmill. Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell and Dexterity (Stealth) checks while resting are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Rest — three weeks; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.
entries.duration: Three weeks, or until cured; the nose stays crooked.

entries.description: The body has not caught up with what happened to it. You gain two levels of exhaustion, removed normally.
entries.cure: Rest — a long rest per level; Lesser Restoration ends it at once.

entries.description: Eight of them, across the forearm. Strength (Athletics) checks are made at disadvantage for a week, and they itch.
Bruised to the bone and stiff with it. Initiative rolls are made at disadvantage.
You cannot fight with two weapons, and attack rolls with a versatile weapon used two-handed are made at disadvantage.
No mechanical effect. Cold drinks hurt and the smile is slightly different.
entries.cure: A tooth-smith's fitting; most people keep it.

entries.description: It bled like a fountain and needed four stitches. No effect after the first day except the bandage, a headache, and a permanent part in your hair.
entries.duration: One week; the part is permanent.

entries.description: Three fingernails ripped back. Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks and checks with thieves' tools are made at disadvantage.
You gain one level of exhaustion, removed normally.
Your speed is reduced by 5 feet.
A burst vessel: one eye is solid red. Charisma (Persuasion) checks are made at disadvantage and Charisma (Intimidation) checks with advantage while it lasts.
You lisp. Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks are made at disadvantage. Verbal components are unaffected, if less dignified.
Eyebrows, lashes and the front of your hair are gone. No mechanical effect; everyone will mention it.
Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing are made at disadvantage.
Attack rolls with two-handed weapons are made at disadvantage.
It bled more than it mattered. No mechanical effect. It will not even scar.

A scar from the corner of the mouth to the ear that no one forgets. Checks to disguise yourself or pass as someone else are made at disadvantage; Charisma (Intimidation) checks against commoners are made with advantage.
entries.notes: Counts as a distinguishing mark on any wanted notice.

entries.description: The upper lip healed with a notch in it. Charisma (Performance) checks to sing are made at disadvantage; nothing else, except that you whistle now whether you mean to or not.
Bitten, frozen or cut off. You breathe through your mouth when you sleep; a distinguishing mark on any wanted notice. No other mechanical effect.
The front ones. Charisma (Persuasion) checks with the gentry are made at disadvantage until a tooth-smith fits ivory; after that, nothing but the whistle.
entries.cure: A tooth-smith's fitting for the Persuasion penalty; Regenerate for the teeth.

entries.injuryType: The Brow That Does Not Move
entries.description: A burn across the forehead tightened the skin: one eyebrow is fixed in place and you read as angry at rest. Charisma (Persuasion) checks with strangers are made at disadvantage and Charisma (Intimidation) checks with advantage.
A ridge of scar from shoulder blade to hip. It pulls in the cold. No mechanical effect except that Charisma (Intimidation) checks are made with advantage when it is on show.

The wound healed in the shape of what made it — a Bob-omb's fuse-burn, a Bullet Bill's rifling, the ring of a Guild sigil, a claw's four lines. Anyone who knows the mark knows the story. No mechanical effect.
entries.notes: Write the thing on the sheet. The GM will use it.

entries.description: Knuckles and palms gone white with old cuts. Charisma (Deception) checks to pass as someone who has never fought are made at disadvantage; Charisma (Persuasion) checks with soldiers, guards and anyone else who reads hands are made with advantage.
The first time you take damage in any combat you must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of the attacker until the end of your next turn.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.
entries.notes: Not funny. Play it straight and let the party cover for them.

entries.description: You wake screaming and you do not go back. At the end of each long rest make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw; on a failure you regain only half the Hit Dice you would have and gain no other benefit from the rest.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.
entries.notes: A trusted ally awake beside the bed gives advantage on the save.

entries.description: Your body decides before you do. Initiative rolls and the first attack roll you make in each combat are made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.

entries.description: Of the thing that did it — fire, deep water, heights, the dark, Bullet Bills, a particular laugh. When you start your turn able to see it you must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of it until the start of your next turn.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.
entries.notes: The GM names the thing from the fiction. It should be something that will come up again.

entries.description: You do not talk about it and you do not talk much. Charisma (Persuasion) checks are made at disadvantage; you cannot be the party's face until this heals.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.

entries.description: You cannot rest where you cannot see the door. A long rest in the open or in an unfamiliar place gives you no benefit unless an ally you trust keeps watch the whole night. While awake you cannot be surprised.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.

entries.description: It comes after, not during. At the end of each combat make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw; on a failure you gain one level of exhaustion, and for the next hour any check that needs steady hands is made at disadvantage.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.

entries.description: Wisdom (Insight) checks are made at disadvantage and Charisma (Intimidation) checks with advantage. When someone insults you to your face you must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or answer in kind, whatever the room.
entries.cure: Care — a season (three months) among people you trust, or Greater Restoration; Calm Emotions quiets it for an hour.

entries.description: The old break aches before rain. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to predict the weather within a day.
A lock of hair, fur or cap-spot went white where the wound was. No mechanical effect; a distinguishing mark on any wanted notice, and a very good story.
The wound aches when the kind of creature or thing that gave it is within 30 feet. The GM rolls in secret: it is right three times in four, and it does not say where.
entries.cure: Remove Curse quiets it, though it is not strictly a curse.

entries.description: It closed under a Star shower, or near something that should not have been glowing. While you are below half your hit points the scar sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius: Dexterity (Stealth) checks in darkness are made at disadvantage, and healers find you very easily.
entries.cure: Remove Curse dims it; Greater Restoration ends it.

entries.description: A hum in the ears whenever a spell is cast within 30 feet. You cannot tell by whom or what, and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing are made at disadvantage until the start of your next turn.
entries.cure: Greater Restoration. Most people keep it.
entries.notes: In the capital, with the Guild everywhere, this is either a warning system or a migraine.

entries.description: A sliver of whatever hit you stayed in, too deep to cut out. Constitution saving throws against lightning damage are made at disadvantage, and Detect Magic shows you faintly.
It closed without a mark, and the hard part taught you something. You have advantage on Wisdom (Medicine) checks to treat the kind of wound you took.
The bone knit thick. Your hit point maximum increases by 2.
You have seen the worst of it and it was survivable. You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
The scar and the story that goes with it. Charisma (Persuasion) checks with soldiers, guards and anyone who has bled for a living are made with advantage.
entries.notes: Free drinks remain the GM's call.

entries.description: Pain is just information now. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration when you take damage.
Your body has learned the trick of not stopping. You succeed on a death saving throw on a roll of 9 or higher.
Once per long rest, when damage would reduce you to 0 hit points but not kill you outright, you drop to 1 hit point instead.
Something — a Star, a Mushroom, pure spite — refused. You wake at your hit point maximum with all your Hit Dice restored and no lasting harm of any kind. It happens once.
entries.notes: Write it in the character file with the date. The table owes you nothing after this.
